usual_baseline: Withdrawal scoring is the weak point. CIWA within 24 hours was 1% [3603]; CIWA-Ar completed 23.97% [3551]; applied 44%, correctly scored 24% [3286]. Complete drinking history 4% [3286]. Physical examination is good at 84–98%, but cognitive assessment before discharge was 7% [3443]. Addiction specialist oversight on acute wards was 4% [3275].
fix_that_works: A ward SOP with risk profiling, nurse-administered CIWA-Ar, a symptom-triggered regimen and front-loading for high risk, after team training [3299]. At re-audit every patient had risk stratification recorded and all got the symptom-triggered regimen. Oral lorazepam fell from 3324 mg for 63 patients to 10 mg for 39 patients.
fix_that_fails: Repeated re-audits at one trust barely moved: CIWA within 24 hours went 1%, then 4%, then 17%; referral to community alcohol services fell to 0% [3603]. Teaching, induction and electronic CIWA-Ar prompts gave better confidence but no figures [3551]. Relapse prevention and specialist referral stayed below 60% [3422].
consultant_advice: Most of these are one-off audits finding the same low CIWA use; only one loop shows a clear gain. Don't just count CIWA scores again. Audit whether a symptom-triggered protocol is followed and changes benzodiazepine doses, or measure referral to community alcohol services and cognitive assessment before discharge, which stay near zero.
